facts.statement: Ankonetta is an extinct genus of birds.
The genus Ankonetta was described by Cenizo and Agnolín in 2010.
The type species of the genus is Ankonetta larriestrai.
Ankonetta was a mid-sized bird belonging to the duck family, Anatidae.
facts.quote: Ankonetta is an extinct genus of mid-sized anatid birds

facts.statement: Fossils of Ankonetta date to the Early Miocene epoch.
The holotype fossil was discovered in the Santa Cruz Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Its holotype was found in the Early Miocene (Santacrucian), Santa Cruz Formation in Argentina

facts.statement: The genus name Ankonetta honors the Aónikenk people of Patagonia.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Aónikenk, a group of indigenous Tehuelche-speaking people from Patagonia

facts.statement: The species name larriestrai honors Claudio Larriestra, a researcher of the Pinturas Formation.
facts.quote: The species epithet refers to Claudio Larriestra, who studied the Pinturas Formation

facts.statement: Ankonetta lived between 23.04 and 15.98 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Burdigalian (23.04 to 15.98 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The second part of the genus name comes from the Greek word for duck.
rejected.quote: netta is derived from Greek, meaning duck
